description: No Montenegro-registered core banking software product vendor was found. All core banking in ME appears to be supplied by foreign/regional vendors, with ME firms acting as integrators, front-end/CRM suppliers or channel operators.

result.result_summary: sr and en queries on 'implementacija core banking sistema Crna Gora integrator' and 'Montenegro core banking implementation references' returned only global vendor/consultancy marketing (Capgemini, Sopra, Temenos lists) and no ME-domiciled core banking supplier or ME-named implementation reference.

why_it_matters: Means the vendor-intelligence signal for core banking in ME must be harvested from bank-side disclosures and regional vendor sites (workstreams other than A6), not from ME corporate reference pages.

description: No Montenegro-based card production or card personalisation bureau identified.

result.result_summary: sr query 'personalizacija kartica Crna Gora kompanija' returned only Serbian bureaus (Cards Print, SIS Kartice, PVC-kartice, MHT) and generic tourism payment pages; no ME-registered personalisation provider surfaced.

why_it_matters: Suggests ME banks source card personalisation cross-border (most likely RS or HR bureaus). Personalisation vendor intelligence for ME therefore has to be collected from Serbian/regional bureau reference pages and from bank card-issuance tender documents.

description: No ME-local authorised distributor/service partner page found for ATM OEMs (NCR/NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Hyosung, GRG).

result.result_summary: sr query mixing OEM names with 'distributer partner Crna Gora bankomati isporuka' returned only global ATM-industry press and parts marketplaces; no ME partner-locator entry surfaced.

why_it_matters: Reinforces the picture that Payten is effectively the single ATM supply-and-service channel in ME. Should be re-tested directly against each OEM's partner-locator page rather than via search engines.

description: Logate's clients page is not at the guessed path.

result.result_summary: https://logate.com/clients/ returned HTTP 404. The equivalent content lives at https://logate.com/case-studies/ and https://logate.com/partners/, confirmed from the site's own navigation.

why_it_matters: Collection configs must use the real /case-studies/ and /partners/ paths; treat the 404 as a path error, not evidence the vendor publishes no references.

description: Several ICT Cortex members plausibly relevant to this cell were not individually opened this run.

result.result_summary: POS4, Financial Solutions, Euro Unit, ZZI, Domen, Codeus, Codelab, OmniTech and VG Group were captured from the cluster directory but only partially or not characterised; their reference pages remain unread.

why_it_matters: The cell's candidate list is therefore a floor, not a ceiling; a second pass opening each cluster member's site would likely add several genuine vendor/reference sources.

description: The routine playbook file on disk could not be consulted.

result.result_summary: The stated playbook path (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/...) is a Windows path and this session runs on macOS; no equivalent local copy was located, so the method followed is the one embedded in the task prompt.

why_it_matters: Any playbook-specific classification conventions or field semantics not restated in the prompt may not be reflected in this slice.

description: No Diebold Nixdorf press release, case study, or partner-locator entry naming Montenegro or a Montenegrin bank was found, in either English or Serbian queries.

result.result_summary: Two searches (en and sr-flavoured) returned only Diebold Nixdorf deployments in Belgium, the Nordics, Antarctica and unnamed 'top-10' institutions. Absence is unverified, not proven — the ME market may be served indirectly through resellers such as Printec or Payten rather than by direct DN contracts.

why_it_matters: If DN has no direct ME presence, the ATM hardware/service competition in Montenegro is effectively a reseller/integrator contest (Payten, Printec, Euronet), which changes who the real competitor set is.

description: No Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra, Backbase, Sopra Banking, BPC SmartVista or OpenWay Way4 customer story naming a Montenegrin bank was located.

result.result_summary: Multiple vendor-scoped and platform-scoped searches returned only generic product/comparison pages and non-ME references (Openbank, Commerce Bank, Tsesnabank).

why_it_matters: Suggests the ME core-banking and card-processing installed base is held by regional vendors (ASEE/Asseco, Payten) and by group-level systems imported from parent banks (NLB, OTP, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat), rather than by direct tier-1 global core vendor contracts. This should be tested against bank annual reports and parent-group IT disclosures.

description: No public partner-locator or reseller-directory entry for Montenegro was found for any of the global vendors in scope (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos, Oracle, Thales, IDEMIA).

result.result_summary: Searches for partner locators returned only Mastercard's Move partner directory (not ME-specific). Vendor partner locators may exist behind JS-driven interfaces that plain web search does not index.

why_it_matters: Partner locators are usually the densest single mapping of a global vendor to its local channel; not finding them via search means they need direct browser-based interrogation rather than search-engine discovery.

description: No vendor named yet for Montenegro's TIPS Clone instant-payments build; the supplier hypothesis (Nexi/SIA, Bankart) is unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: CBCG material identifies Banca d'Italia and the World Bank as counterparties and a mid-2026 target, and an open RFB for 'TIPS Clone Connectivity Services', but names no technology supplier.

why_it_matters: The largest payments-infrastructure programme in the market currently has no attributable vendor; whoever wins the connectivity and bank-side adaptation work gains a durable position with all ME banks.

description: No Worldline, Nexi, Ingenico or Verifone page referencing Montenegro operations, an ME merchant-acquiring business, or an ME terminal contract was found.

result.result_summary: Searches returned only pan-European market-structure material and the Worldline/Ingenico merger documentation.

why_it_matters: Indicates ME acquiring is bank-owned and locally serviced rather than outsourced to a pan-European acquirer — a structurally different competitive landscape from Croatia or Serbia.

description: Serbian/Montenegrin-language searching produced far fewer vendor-side results than English, because international vendors publish ME wins in English on their global sites, not in sr.

result.result_summary: sr queries ('Crna Gora banka implementirala rješenje dobavljač saopštenje', 'Asseco SEE Crna Gora Podgorica banka projekat') returned bank and central-bank pages rather than vendor pages; the productive sr surfaces were vendor local sites (euronetatms.me), bank product pages, and bankar.me.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for vendor-side evidence English is the primary language, while sr is needed to reach vendor local subsidiaries, job ads and bank-side technology fingerprints. Collection must run both, with different source lists.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin banking or payments industry AWARD programme was found — no local equivalent of a 'nagrada za najbolje digitalno bankarsko rješenje' or a national fintech award with a published shortlist.

result.result_summary: Local-language award searches returned only (a) CBCG's annual academic/scientific-thought prize (godišnja nagrada CBCG, a research competition, not a product award) and (b) foreign awards conferred on ME banks (The Banker, Global Finance). No ME-run shortlist naming vendors was located.

why_it_matters: Award shortlists were expected to be a cheap vendor-partnership signal for this cell; in ME that signal must instead be recovered from foreign award citations plus the winning bank's own press release.

description: bankar.me, the most on-point local banking trade portal, returned HTTP 403 to a direct fetch of its Konferencije category page.

result.result_summary: WebFetch of https://bankar.me/category/edukacija/konferencije/ -> 403 Forbidden. Individual article URLs on the same domain appear in search indexes and were readable via search snippets, so the site is presumed live and bot-defended rather than dead.

why_it_matters: This is a high-value source; collection design must budget for a browser-context or header-realistic fetcher rather than a plain HTTP client. Recorded as unverified, NOT dead.

description: No banking or payments conference or expo was found that is held specifically in Bar or Budva with a banking/payments focus, despite that being named in the cell scope.

result.result_summary: Searches combining Budva/Bečići/Bar with bankarstvo/fintech/konferencija surfaced only general business/tech events (Spark.me in Budva, ConfCoast, IT 2026 academic conference) and the Tivat/Porto Montenegro INFINTECH. No Bar-based financial event located.

why_it_matters: Narrows the ME event universe: for banking/payments specifically, the venue set is effectively Tivat/Porto Montenegro (INFINTECH) and Podgorica (SCMN conference, FID, IT SPOT), so monitoring can be tightly scoped.

description: INFINTECH's sponsor block renders several sponsor names only as logo images; text extraction recovered Platinum (Capsys, Green Printec) and Silver (Porto Montenegro) but left Gold tier and two Silver/partner slots unnamed.

result.result_summary: Fetched https://infintech.me/ — '30+ Speakers', Platinum/Gold/Silver tiers present, Gold tier described as three companies with logos only.

why_it_matters: The most valuable field in this cell (who is at which sponsor tier) is partially image-encoded; the collector must OCR or inspect image alt/filename attributes, not just parse text.

description: No archive of past INFINTECH editions (2023/2024/2025 sponsor and speaker rosters) was found on the current infintech.me site.

result.result_summary: The live site presents only the 2026 edition; no /past-events/ or year-archive path was surfaced. ME press coverage (bankar.me on Infintech 2025) is currently the only pointer to prior editions.

why_it_matters: Year-over-year sponsor diffing — the core analytic value of this cell — cannot be done from the live site alone and depends on the Internet Archive plus press recaps.

description: No evidence found that a 'Banking 4.0' or 'Payments SEE' branded event has a Montenegro edition or a Montenegro-specific track.

result.result_summary: Searches for these named formats plus Montenegro returned only global conference-calendar aggregators and Croatian Money Motion; no ME edition or ME speaker track surfaced.

why_it_matters: Regional coverage for ME should be anchored on Money Motion (Zagreb) and BANCEE rather than the Romanian Banking 4.0 franchise assumed in the seed queries.

description: No established Montenegrin-language term was found for 'exhibitor list' as a standalone published artefact in the ME event ecosystem.

result.result_summary: 'Izlagači' returns fair/trade-show usage; ME banking events publish 'sponzori' and 'partneri' pages but generally not an 'izlagači' page, because these are conference-format not expo-format events.

why_it_matters: Collection queries and page-path heuristics should target /sponzori/, /partneri/, /sponsors/, /partners/ rather than exhibitor paths; assuming an exhibitor list exists will produce false 'missing page' signals.

description: No Montenegrin media article naming a specific core-banking or payments vendor under contract with a named Montenegrin bank was surfaced, despite targeted sr queries combining bank names with Asseco/ASEE, Halcom, and generic 'dobavljač'/'tehnološki partner' phrasing.

result.result_summary: Queries returned infrastructure-level coverage (SEPA, TIPS Clone, FinTech Strategy 2025-2029) and institutional actors (CBCG, Bank of Italy, World Bank, EPC), but no article-level bank-to-vendor contract attribution.

why_it_matters: Vendor attribution in ME appears to live inside interviews, conference coverage and vendor-side press rather than in news headlines — so the collection design must prioritise Bankar.me interviews and event write-ups over generic news crawling, and must be paired with vendor-side and tender sources from other cells.

description: Neither vijesti.me nor a separate 'Bankar Magazin' print edition was confirmed by an actually-retrieved page in this run.

result.result_summary: Vijesti appears only as a Wikipedia entry in the result sets; 'Bankar Magazin' as a distinct print product separate from the bankar.me portal was not evidenced. Bankar.me itself is well confirmed.

why_it_matters: Two named cell targets remain unverified. Vijesti is likely the single highest-value general outlet for contract reporting, so failing to confirm its section structure leaves a real gap; the print magazine, if it exists, may carry CIO interviews never posted online.

description: Direct automated fetch of the Bankar.me Montenegro-banking category returned HTTP 403.

result.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on WebFetch; the same domain's article URLs appear consistently and recently in search indexes, so the site is live and bot-defended rather than down.

why_it_matters: The single most valuable source in this cell will need a headless-browser or header-spoofing collector, or an RSS path, and must not be marked dead by a naive liveness check.

description: Local IT vendors serving Montenegrin banks were only partially mapped; Logate (Podgorica IT company, organiser of the Infintech conference) surfaced, but the wider domestic supplier set was not enumerated.

result.result_summary: One domestic vendor identified via conference coverage; search budget was exhausted before a dedicated vendor-side sweep could run.

why_it_matters: Domestic integrators are frequently the actual implementers behind bank platform stories in small markets; without their inventory, media mentions cannot be resolved to suppliers.

description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted mid-cell, cutting off planned sweeps of Logate/Infintech vendor coverage, RTCG/antenam/aktuelno banking sections, and Standard (standard.co.me).

result.result_summary: Last two planned sr queries were refused by the search tool.

why_it_matters: Cell coverage is good but not exhaustive; a follow-up run with fresh budget should complete the vendor-side and second-tier-outlet sweeps.

description: Halcom's publicly published customer bank list (fetched) enumerates Slovenia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Albania, but contains no Montenegro section or Montenegrin bank.

result.result_summary: No ME entry found on the vendor's own customer list at the time of this run.

why_it_matters: Suggests Halcom has no (or unpublished) Montenegrin bank footprint — a whitespace signal, and a reminder that some regional vendors genuinely skip ME rather than serving it quietly.

description: Searches in both Serbian and English for a named regional-integrator case study describing a specific Montenegrin bank project (core banking, cards, channels) returned only generic claims (e.g. ASEE stating Basel/IFRS9 implementations across a country list including Montenegro) — no discrete, citable ME reference page was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Country-list-level claims only; no per-project ME case study surfaced.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell hypothesis that ME references are aggregated into regional country lists rather than published as standalone references — collection must therefore parse country lists and app metadata, not hunt for case-study pages.

description: No evidence found linking Bosnian integrators Lanaco, Prointer or M&I Systems (and their BiH peers) to Montenegrin bank projects, in either language.

result.result_summary: Search returned no BiH-vendor-to-ME-bank connections.

why_it_matters: The Sarajevo/Banja Luka spillover leg of this cell is currently unevidenced; either the channel does not exist or these vendors publish nothing. Needs a dedicated pass on BiH vendor sites and BiH tech media before concluding.

description: The term 'Adriatic' is heavily polluted: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica (a Montenegrin bank) dominates English-language results for 'Adriatic ... Montenegro bank', crowding out genuine Adriatic-region vendor content. Similarly 'Crna Gora' collides with 'Razvojna banka Crne Gore' and 'Centralna banka Crne Gore' regulatory documents.

result.result_summary: Query noise identified; English 'Adriatic region vendor' queries produced almost no vendor-side results.

why_it_matters: Future query design must pair 'Adria/Adriatic/regionalni' with vendor-side terms (integrator, implementacija, reference, isporučilac, rješenje) and negative-filter the bank name.

description: Run languages were limited to sr and en; Croatian-specific phrasing (rješenje/rješenja vs rešenje, 'referentna lista', 'implementacija u banci') was only partially exercised, and no dedicated hr-language query set was run against Croatian vendor sites (Combis, King ICT, Span, Multicom, Infobip).

result.result_summary: Croatian-language coverage incomplete by design of the run scope.

why_it_matters: Zagreb is one of the three cities from which ME is served; missing hr-language coverage likely under-counts Croatian vendors' ME references.

description: Targeted local-language query combining Montenegrin job-ad terms with named core-banking products ("Crna Gora" banka posao "Asseco" OR "Oracle Flexcube" OR "Pexim" OR "Temenos" iskustvo oglas) returned only generic vendor encyclopaedia pages and non-ME job ads.

result.result_summary: No Montenegrin job advertisement naming a specific core-banking platform was surfaced through general web search this run.

why_it_matters: The cell's central hypothesis — that ME bank job ads name their core platform — is untested. It likely requires site-internal search of zzzcg.me/srm and bank ATS pages rather than general web search, since those bodies are poorly indexed.

description: LinkedIn company pages and vendor posts tagging Montenegrin clients could not be inspected; the platform is auth-walled and its terms prohibit automated collection.

result.result_summary: Only the CKB Bank company-page URL was recoverable; no post content read.

why_it_matters: Vendor-tags-client LinkedIn posts are one of the two named pillars of this cell. Without a manual analyst seat or a licensed provider, this channel stays effectively closed.

description: The Administrative Court (Upravni sud Crne Gore) appeal layer above procurement-commission decisions, and the central e-procurement system (CEJN / ESJN) contract-award records, were queued but not searched — the session's web-search budget was exhausted (200/200 calls) before those queries ran.

result.result_summary: Two planned local-language queries were not executed.

why_it_matters: Upravni sud rulings and CEJN award notices are the two remaining high-yield public windows into contested and awarded ME banking/IT tenders; the appeals database alone gives only the first instance.

description: No GitHub organisation, public repository, or technology-stack fingerprint source specific to Montenegrin banks or their local integrators was identified. No local-language term exists for this channel; the search vocabulary is inherently English/technical.

result.result_summary: GitHub / tech-stack fingerprinting sub-channel of the cell remains unpopulated.

why_it_matters: Mandatory local-language coverage is not achievable for this sub-channel, and it was not covered in English either — a real hole in the cell.

description: The CKB careers ATS page returned only its client-side shell on fetch; department filters including 'IT i operacije' were visible but no job bodies.

result.result_summary: Source confirmed to exist and to be structured usefully, but content not readable without JS rendering.

why_it_matters: Signals that bank-side ATS pages across ME will generally need a headless browser or the ATS vendor's public JSON API, which changes the collection design for this whole source family.

description: No Montenegro-specific EY 'Banking Barometer' or SEE banking barometer edition was located. EY Banking Barometer editions found are Switzerland/Liechtenstein; the EY-IIF risk survey is global.

result.result_summary: Seed-query assumption of an 'EY/Deloitte SEE banking barometer' covering ME is not confirmed; regional coverage appears to run through Deloitte CE/CEE surveys and EY Adriatic content instead.

why_it_matters: Avoids a false expectation of a recurring ME-specific benchmark study; collection should instead target regional CEE surveys and grep for Montenegro mentions.

description: No KPMG Montenegro legal entity appeared in the ICAM register of 37 licensed audit firms returned, and no ME-locale KPMG site was confirmed.

result.result_summary: Of the Big-4, Deloitte DOO, Ernst & Young Montenegro DOO and PricewaterhouseCoopers DOO are confirmed on the Montenegrin audit-firm register; KPMG was not observed there.

why_it_matters: Changes the adviser actor map: statutory bank audits in ME are likely split among three Big-4 firms plus mid-tier (BDO, Crowe MNE, HLB Mont Audit, TPA), which narrows who to monitor.

description: Planned queries on EBRD Montenegro financial-sector diagnostics and on rating-agency (Moody's/S&P/Fitch) reports on Montenegrin banks could not be run.

result.result_summary: WebSearch session budget (200/200) was exhausted after four queries in this slice; EBRD and rating-agency candidates are therefore inferred rather than observed.

why_it_matters: Two named components of the cell brief (EBRD assessments, credit-rating bank reports) are under-evidenced and must be re-scouted in a follow-up run.

description: No publicly indexed Montenegrin bank external-auditor report explicitly describing an 'informacioni sistem' / IT-controls review was surfaced; the sr query returned the statutory framework and the CBCG repository instead.

result.result_summary: IT-controls findings, if published at all, are embedded inside the audited financial statements PDFs on cbcg.me and individual bank sites rather than as standalone documents.

why_it_matters: Collection must be full-text PDF parsing of bank annual reports, not URL-pattern discovery of separate IT-audit reports.

description: The session's web-search quota (200/200) was consumed before the cell's later query lines could be run, specifically the Uprava za digitalizaciju i informacionu bezbjednost / implementer queries and the English 'Montenegro e-government payment implementer' query.

result.result_summary: Only 4 of the planned ~12 queries executed (3 sr, 1 mixed). Coverage of the state-digital-counterpart half of the cell is therefore shallower than the archive half.

why_it_matters: The implementers named in digital-agenda execution records are the highest-value output of this cell and remain largely unenumerated.

description: Fetched https://www.gov.me/clanak/sistem-za-elektronsko-placanje in full; it names the system (NS NAT) and the owning ministry but discloses no vendor, integrator, acquirer bank, funding source or dates.

result.result_summary: State e-payment implementer not identified from the government's own description page.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise: the implementer must be recovered from procurement records, gazette decisions or archived vendor case studies rather than from the counterpart's public page.

description: The Strategija digitalne transformacije 2022–2026 PDF (2.2MB, ntpark.me mirror) downloaded successfully but remote text conversion returned unusable output; institutions, budgets and system lists could not be extracted in this pass.

result.result_summary: Key strategy document acquired but unparsed. This is an extraction problem, not a dead source.

why_it_matters: That document is the single richest listing of planned state information systems and e-payment workstreams for this cell.

description: The sr query aimed at archived Montenegrin vendor/bank reference pages returned only live institutional pages and a browser extension listing — no specific archived case-study URLs. General web search does not index Wayback snapshot URLs well.

result.result_summary: Archived vendor case studies must be reached through the CDX API against a pre-built actor/domain list, not through search engines.

why_it_matters: Sets the collection design: build the actor map first (CBCG bank register + CRPS + tender awards), then archive-enumerate each domain.

description: No Montenegrin national web-archiving programme (an equivalent of a legal-deposit web archive at the Nacionalna biblioteka Crne Gore 'Đurđe Crnojević' or Državni arhiv Crne Gore) was located in this pass; local terms 'nacionalna biblioteka', 'državni arhiv', 'obavezni primjerak' were not searched due to the budget cut-off.

result.result_summary: Unverified whether a domestic .me web archive exists as an alternative to Wayback.

why_it_matters: If one exists it would hold captures Wayback missed for small local vendor sites; if not, Wayback is a single point of failure for this cell.

description: sluzbenilist.me exposes issue-level registry pages via opaque GUID URLs; whether a full-text search endpoint over all issues exists was not established.

result.result_summary: Systematic keyword retrieval across the gazette is not yet proven feasible.

why_it_matters: Without full-text search, gazette monitoring degrades to per-issue enumeration, which is far costlier.

description: Repeated sr-language searching for 'novosti' / 'obavještenja' / 'saopštenja' scoped to Zapad banka, Universal Capital Bank and Lovćen banka returned no indexed news-section URL for any of the three. Only corporate/about pages and third-party directory profiles surfaced.

result.result_summary: No newsroom URL confirmed for 3 of the 10 banks in this cell. Their websites may carry an unindexed news path, or they may genuinely publish only via social channels.

why_it_matters: If the smaller banks have no newsroom, the entire disclosure burden for them shifts to social feeds and vendor case studies — which changes the collection design from crawling to analyst-assisted monitoring.

description: Across every query in both languages, not one Montenegrin bank press release was found that explicitly names its core-banking, card-processing or channel technology supplier in prose. The Adriatic Bank Apple Pay launch, the most prominent 2025 ME retail-payments announcement located, was reported without any implementation-partner attribution.

result.result_summary: Zero prose-level vendor attributions from the buyer side; all supplier attribution obtained in this pass came from indirect artifacts (app package ids, vendor case studies, shared service-centre sites).

why_it_matters: Confirms and sharpens the cell rationale: the buyer side is a first-class channel for detecting THAT something was bought and WHEN, but almost never WHO supplied it. Vendor-side and technical-artifact sources must carry the attribution.

description: Three fetch attempts failed in this pass: https://www.ckb.me/ (TLS 'unable to verify the first certificate'), https://www.hipotekarnabanka.com/obavjestenja/ (404 on the bare section index), and https://www.nlb.me/novosti (404 on a guessed path).

result.result_summary: All three are hypotheses about the fetcher or the URL guess, not verdicts about the sites. CKB and Hipotekarna both have indexed live content under those same domains/paths.

why_it_matters: A downstream liveness pass must not mark these dead. CKB needs a fetcher with a complete CA bundle; Hipotekarna needs item-level URLs rather than the section index; NLB's news path must be discovered from site navigation rather than guessed.

description: The Hipotekarna Banka on-site search endpoint (https://hipotekarnabanka.com/pretraga/?q=...) reflects arbitrary query strings into indexed pages, and an indexed result was found containing unrelated injected Korean-language spam text rather than bank content.

result.result_summary: The bank's own search endpoint has been abused for SEO spam injection.

why_it_matters: Any collector crawling that endpoint will ingest attacker-controlled text under a trusted bank domain. Content retrieved from /pretraga/ must be treated as untrusted data and excluded from vendor-mention extraction; only canonical /obavjestenja/ item pages should feed the pipeline.

description: No Montenegrin/Serbian-language equivalent term was found in use by the banks for supplier-facing concepts such as 'technology partner' or 'implementation partner'. Bank communications use generic terms ('rješenje', 'novi sistem', 'u saradnji sa') rather than any consistent procurement vocabulary.

result.result_summary: There is no reliable sr-language keyword that isolates vendor-disclosure content; keyword-only filtering will under-recall.

why_it_matters: Collection must not rely on sr keyword matching for vendor detection. Full-text ingestion plus named-entity recognition against a maintained vendor gazetteer (Asseco/ASEE, Logate, Fleka, Halcom, ProvisionPay, Bankart, e-mon) is required instead.

description: Several cell terms are heavily polluted in search. 'Novosti' collides with the Serbian newspapers Novosti a.d. and Večernje novosti and the Croatian weekly Novosti; 'Vijesti' collides with the major Montenegrin daily Vijesti; 'Nova Banka' collides with the Bosnian bank of the same name (Adriatic Bank's former name); 'Komercijalna banka' collides with Serbian and Bosnian entities; 'Hipotekarna' collides with Banco Hipotecario.

result.result_summary: Unqualified local-language queries return substantial off-target results, including Wikipedia articles about unrelated media outlets and banks.

why_it_matters: All sr queries in this cell must be domain-scoped or co-constrained with 'Crna Gora'/'Podgorica'/'.me' to be usable; otherwise both search-based discovery and any automated relevance scoring will be badly degraded.

description: Consistent with the cell rationale, no public tender, RFP or contract-award record was located for any commercial bank in Montenegro. The banks are private entities outside the public-procurement regime.

result.result_summary: No procurement-portal source exists for this cell; only the state-adjacent Central Bank of Montenegro would publish tenders, and that is outside this cell's buyer set.

why_it_matters: Confirms there is no shortcut. The collection design must accept that timing and attribution will be reconstructed from launch communications, financial-statement intangibles, app artifacts and vendor self-reporting rather than from any authoritative award record.

description: No public procurement / supplier ('nabavke', 'dobavljači', 'javni pozivi') section could be located for any Montenegrin private bank — CKB, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank AD Podgorica, Addiko ME, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, Prva banka, UCB, Adriatic, Ziraat — despite site-scoped and entity-scoped searching in Montenegrin.

result.result_summary: Searches returned corporate/product pages, press releases and property-sale oglasi, but no standing tender page. CKB was observed issuing a 'javni poziv' via Facebook rather than a procurement webpage.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise: private-bank buying in ME is invitation-based and does not leave a standing public trail. Collection must pivot to press oglasi, social channels, group parents and IFI portals rather than bank websites.

description: No NLB Group supplier/vendor portal or 'postani dobavitelj' page was found in Slovenian or English.

result.result_summary: Slovenian-language querying ('dobavitelji', 'nabave', 'javna naročila') returned NLB's supplier-factoring product and unrelated Croatian public-procurement material; no group sourcing entry point.

why_it_matters: Of the three group parents, NLB is the one with no visible external sourcing gateway — meaning NLB Banka Podgorica's vendor selection is the least observable of the group-owned banks and needs a different approach (people, press, references).

description: etenderi.me refused connection and bankar.me returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch.

result.result_summary: etenderi.me: ECONNREFUSED on https; bankar.me: 403 Forbidden. Both appear in search indexes with recent content.

why_it_matters: These are two of the highest-value local sources in the cell; both need browser-grade collection (headless browser, realistic headers) or a subscription rather than plain HTTP fetching. Neither should be recorded as dead.

description: Commercial global aggregators (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, MontenegroTenders, TendersOnTime) advertise 'private tenders' coverage for Montenegro, but no instance of a genuine Montenegrin private-bank tender in their indexes was observed.

result.result_summary: Marketing copy asserts private-sector coverage; no verifying example surfaced in search results.

why_it_matters: Buying a subscription on that promise is a real risk of spend with no incremental coverage of the private-bank route this cell exists to cover.

description: No evidence found that OTP Group's supplier programme or SAP Ariba rollout explicitly extends to, or publishes notices for, CKB Banka Montenegro.

result.result_summary: The OTP suppliers page describes registration via vendorman@otpbank.hu, a phased Ariba rollout, a Partner Code of Ethics and DORA ICT-security training, but says nothing about subsidiary scope.

why_it_matters: Whether CKB buys through Budapest or locally determines the entire collection strategy for Montenegro's largest bank; this is the single highest-value open question in the cell.

description: cejn.gov.me — the canonical source for this cell — is a client-side-rendered SPA. Both https://cejn.gov.me/tenders and a concrete tender page https://cejn.gov.me/tenders/view-tender/103145 returned only the literal token 'CeJN' via plain HTTP fetch.

result.result_summary: No server-side HTML; no API endpoint identified in this pass. This is a rendering barrier, NOT evidence the portal is down — search engines index individual view-tender URLs, so the portal is presumed live and unverified.

why_it_matters: The primary hard-evidence source cannot be collected with simple HTTP fetching; the pipeline needs a headless browser or a reverse-engineered JSON API, otherwise collection silently degrades to the third-party mirror.

description: No open, machine-readable bulk dataset or open-data dump of Montenegrin procurement awards (OCDS-style) was found. Unlike Serbia/BiH, ME appears to expose data only through the CeJN UI, and no data.gov.me procurement dataset surfaced.

result.result_summary: Searches for a ME procurement API/open-data feed returned only portal UIs, commercial aggregators and NGO analyses.

why_it_matters: Longitudinal competitor-share analysis for the public slice will require self-built extraction and normalisation rather than dataset ingestion; budget accordingly.

description: No concrete ME award notice specifically for ATMs (bankomati) or bank card/cash-handling infrastructure was surfaced in this discovery pass — only an adjacent transit 'smart POS terminal validator' procurement (Glavni grad Podgorica) and IT/maintenance contracts (SAP Trezor, CBCG printing).

result.result_summary: Local-language queries using 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'nabavka' returned the portal and legal framework rather than matching award documents.

why_it_matters: Either ME state buyers rarely tender ATM/card hardware (commercial banks buy it privately, outside the procurement regime), or such notices exist only inside the CeJN SPA and are invisible to search engines. Both readings materially change how much of the ME market this cell can actually see; must be resolved by an in-portal keyword search.

description: https://www.nabavke.com/javne-nabavke-tenderi-crna-gora/ (aggregator country landing path) returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch, while deep per-tender URLs under the same prefix are indexed and reachable.

result.result_summary: Path is a URL-segment prefix rather than a browsable index; recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: Crawler seeding must start from search-engine-discovered deep links or the site's own search UI, not from a guessed listing root.

description: Montenegrin/Serbian coverage was strong across all subqueries; however no Albanian-language (sq) procurement channel was sought or found, despite a significant Albanian-speaking population in ME (Ulcinj, Tuzi, Plav).

result.result_summary: All local-language searching in this pass was sr/Montenegrin Latin; en used only for IFI sources.

why_it_matters: Municipal-level notices in Albanian-majority municipalities could be missed, though CeJN publication is in Montenegrin so the risk is low.

description: No TED contract notice or award specifically for a Montenegrin banking/core-banking or payment information system funded by IPA surfaced in general web search.

result.result_summary: General web search returns only TED platform documentation, not ME-specific banking notices; TED's own faceted search or API is required because notice text is not well indexed by general engines.

why_it_matters: Confirms that TED must be queried through its native search/API rather than via search engines, otherwise ME financial-sector notices will be systematically missed.

description: EBRD Montenegro results were dominated by non-financial-sector assignments (PIU support/mobility consultancy); no EBRD financial-sector systems contract award for ME was located.

result.result_summary: Only one concrete ME award found (MC Mobility Consultants GmbH, PIU establishment/training, EUR 225,900, signed 06/05/2025) — transport, not finance.

why_it_matters: EBRD's ME financial-sector activity may run through credit lines to banks (no public procurement) rather than procured systems contracts, so ECEPP should be monitored but weighted lower than World Bank/TED.

description: No KfW-financed financial-sector procurement notice for Montenegro was found; KfW's visible ME footprint in results is energy (HPP Perućica).

result.result_summary: KfW appears as buyer only for an energy tender; financial cooperation with ME banks does not appear to generate public procurement notices.

why_it_matters: Prevents over-investing collection effort in a low-yield channel; KfW stays as low-priority monitoring.

description: Montenegrin/Serbian-language searching surfaces national procurement vocabulary well but almost never surfaces supranational award notices, because funders publish awards in English only.

result.result_summary: sr queries using 'javna nabavka', 'ugovor', 'obavještenje', 'platni promet', 'informacioni sistem' returned national portals, aggregators and EU Delegation news, not IFI award records.

why_it_matters: Local-language collection for this cell should target beneficiary-side confirmation (ministries, CBCG, press) rather than the award records themselves, which must be collected in English.

description: IFC Disclosure Portal was inferred as a required channel from first principles but no Montenegro financial-institution disclosure page was actually retrieved in this pass.

result.result_summary: Listed as a candidate with reduced confidence; no example_urls recorded because none were observed.

why_it_matters: Downstream verification must confirm the ME/FI filter yields records before this source is promoted.

description: No evidence found of a Montenegro-domiciled, independent (non-bank) card acquirer or domestic card processor operating its own switch; card acceptance appears to run through bank acquiring arms plus regional/foreign gateways.

result.result_summary: Searches in sr and en for local akvajering/procesiranje companies returned only bank product pages, regional gateways (Monri, CorvusPay, AllSecure) and Payten's Podgorica entity.

why_it_matters: If confirmed, the ME acquiring value chain is bank-owned with outsourced processing — meaning competitive displacement happens at the bank-vendor contract level, not at the PSP level.

description: No Montenegro-specific merchant case-study or reference pages were located on any PSP/processor site during this pass.

result.result_summary: Payten, Monri and CorvusPay publish regional product content; the only ME-relevant merchant reference surfaced was the Monri–Glovo BiH/ME partnership reported in media, not on a vendor case-study page.

why_it_matters: Merchant-reference intelligence for ME will have to come from media, integrator sites and gateway fingerprints on merchant checkout pages rather than vendor case libraries.

description: The contents of the CBCG payment-institution and e-money registers (the actual entity lists) were not retrieved in this pass — only the register landing pages were identified.

result.result_summary: Register index page fetched successfully and four register URLs confirmed; individual register contents not opened.

why_it_matters: The actual named entities are the core deliverable of this cell; a follow-up fetch is required before any actor map can be considered complete.

description: AllSecure, Novalnet and directory-listed providers claim or imply Montenegro coverage, but no ME licence, ME bank partnership or ME merchant was confirmed for them.

result.result_summary: Marketing-page claims only; nothing corroborated against CBCG registers.

why_it_matters: Treating aggregator/marketing claims as market presence would inflate the perceived competitive set; all such names need register cross-checks.

description: No published merchant discount rate / MDR or acquiring fee schedule was found for ME acquirers in this pass.

result.result_summary: Bank POS and e-commerce pages describe the service but were not observed to publish MDR; CKB publishes general terms PDFs which may contain some fee data (unverified).

why_it_matters: Pricing benchmarking for ME acquiring will likely require tariff PDFs ('tarifnik', 'opšti uslovi') per bank rather than product pages.

description: Searched in both Montenegrin and English for a national card switch / domestic scheme operator in Montenegro (e.g. an equivalent of Serbia's DinaCard or BiH's BH mreža). No such operator was found. The World Bank FSAP technical note instead describes an interoperable ATM/POS network whose routing and settlement occur over the international card scheme networks.

result.result_summary: No domestic card scheme or national switch operator identified for ME; card routing appears to run entirely on Visa/Mastercard rails, with CBCG's RTGS/DNS as the only interbank infrastructure.

why_it_matters: Removes an entire hypothesised actor class from the cell and reframes the vendor question: card-side technology decisions sit with individual banks and their processors, not with a national switch operator, so the leverage point is the CBCG platform plus per-bank processing contracts.

description: Mastercard's Europe newsroom and Visa's public channels were searched in English for Montenegro-specific partnership, launch or certification announcements naming a Montenegrin bank. Nothing Montenegro-specific surfaced in search results; hits were global or other-market items.

result.result_summary: No ME-specific Visa or Mastercard press announcement found in this pass.

why_it_matters: The scheme-newsroom channel, though conceptually the highest-leverage pointer, appears to be low-yield for a market of Montenegro's size. Collection should treat it as a low-frequency monitor rather than a primary feed, and weight CBCG/UBCG/bank channels higher.

description: No Montenegrin-language Visa or Mastercard country page or local newsroom for Montenegro was found. Local-language terms used included 'kartična šema', 'Visa kartice Crna Gora', 'Mastercard Crna Gora'; results returned only bank product pages (Addiko, Erste, Prva banka, CKB), not scheme-operated local channels.

result.result_summary: Schemes appear to have no ME-localised publishing channel; local scheme-related content lives on issuer bank sites instead.

why_it_matters: Means scheme signals for ME must be picked up either from regional/European scheme channels or reconstructed from issuer bank communications and general terms & conditions documents.

description: Searched in Montenegrin for the card-processing supplier behind Montenegrin banks (Payten / Asseco SEE / MultiCard / Chip Card terms). Regional evidence for these vendors exists (Payten as part of Asseco SEE; MultiCard consortium in Serbia), but no result explicitly tied any of them to a Montenegrin bank's processing.

result.result_summary: Regional processor candidates identified but no confirmed ME engagement in this pass.

why_it_matters: The bank-by-bank processing vendor map for ME remains open and must be built from bank T&Cs, annual reports, procurement records and vendor reference pages rather than from a single pointer source.

description: No Montenegro-specific SWIFT country/user-group source was located in this pass. Searches focused on SEPA and TIPS; a SWIFT national member/user group (NMG) page or ME BIC directory view was not confirmed.

result.result_summary: SWIFT-side sourcing for ME is an untested branch, recorded as unverified rather than absent.

why_it_matters: SWIFT adhesion, ISO 20022 CBPR+ migration and BIC directory data are complementary evidence of which ME institutions connect internationally and which service bureaux serve them.

description: The routine playbook path given in the brief (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/... routine_prompt.md) is a Windows path and is not present on this macOS host, so the full method document could not be read. Work proceeded from the instructions embedded in the brief.

result.result_summary: Playbook unavailable on this machine.

why_it_matters: Some playbook-specific conventions (scoring calibration, subtype taxonomy) may not be exactly matched in this slice.

description: No dedicated CBCG register of card processors / card-acquiring processors or ATM operators was found as a distinct published list. Searches in sr for processing and exchange-office terminology returned only the four payment-side registers plus the bank register.

result.result_summary: Card processing appears to be covered implicitly, either inside the 'registar platnih sistema' (system operators) or as an authorised service line within the payment-institution register, rather than as a separate list.

why_it_matters: Cell #9's remit explicitly names card processors; if no discrete register exists, downstream cells cannot derive processor actors from a register and must infer them from payment-system operator entries plus CRPS activity codes.

description: Search for a register of authorised exchange offices ('registar ovlašćenih mjenjača', 'mjenjački poslovi') on cbcg.me returned no such list.

result.result_summary: Only the payment registers and generic financial-system pages were returned; no exchange-office register surfaced.

why_it_matters: Exchange offices are a cash-handling channel adjacent to payments; their absence from the enumerable set is a coverage limitation to state explicitly rather than assume away.

description: The guessed English-language CBCG URL https://www.cbcg.me/en/key-functions/payment-system/registers/register-of-payment-institutions-and-their-agents returned HTTP 404.

result.result_summary: CBCG does not use translated English URL slugs; the English tree reuses the Montenegrin slugs under an /eng/ prefix (confirmed by an observed /eng/kljucne-funkcije/... bank-register URL).

why_it_matters: Any crawler built on translated English paths will silently miss the entire English mirror. Locale handling must be prefix-swap, not slug translation. This is a URL-construction failure, not evidence the English register is missing.

description: The IRMS tax-portal business-entity register search rendered no content to a plain HTTP fetch.

result.result_summary: Only the 'IRMS Portal' shell was returned; the register UI is client-side rendered.

why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified/hypothesis, not dead. It likely has an underlying JSON API that would be the best structured collection route for ME company data — worth a headless-browser investigation.

description: For both the Capital Market Authority (scmn.me) and the Insurance Supervision Agency (ano.me), the existence of a licence register was confirmed in their own descriptive material, but the direct public register URL was not established in this pass.

result.result_summary: Regulator homepages and rules pages located; register deep-links not located.

why_it_matters: These two supervisors cover investment firms and insurers, adjacent buyer segments. Leaving them at homepage granularity weakens the completeness claim of the licensed-actor index.

description: No public structured member directory ('imenik članova') was located for Privredna komora Crne Gore despite a targeted sr-language search.

result.result_summary: Only institutional pages (about, boards, contact) surfaced; no searchable member database.

why_it_matters: The chamber would otherwise be the natural industry-side cross-check on the ICT vendor population; without it, vendor enumeration depends more heavily on CRPS activity codes.

description: data.gov.me was confirmed to exist as a national open-data portal, but no specific CRPS, CBCG-register or licensed-institution dataset was confirmed to be published there in this pass.

result.result_summary: Portal and a 'uprava' dataset group were located; the presence of a machine-readable company or licence register dataset remains unverified.

why_it_matters: If such a dataset exists it would replace fragile HTML/PDF scraping with a legal, structured feed. Its absence would mean all register collection must be scrape-based.

description: No dedicated Montenegrin fintech or payments-industry association was found in either sr or en searching ('fintech asocijacija', 'udruženje', 'payments association').

result.result_summary: Searches returned only the PKCG banking/finance board, UBCG, and a newly formed CFO association; no fintech/payments trade body exists or is publicly visible.

why_it_matters: Payments-vendor intelligence in ME must be reconstructed from the bank association, the chamber's finance board and the ICT cluster rather than from a single industry body.

description: Two navigation URLs surfaced by search returned HTTP 404 on fetch: https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenja-2 and https://www.amcham.me/members/.

result.result_summary: 404 on both; working equivalents appear to be https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenja and https://www.amcham.me/en/member-list (the latter taken from the live amcham.me homepage navigation, not yet fetched).

why_it_matters: Both sites have recently been restructured; any stored crawl paths for chamber/AmCham directories will need re-derivation rather than being treated as dead sources.

description: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore (UPCG) and Montenegro Business Alliance do not publish an itemised member-company list on the open web.

result.result_summary: UPCG publishes board composition and membership categories only; MBA's claimed 500+ members appear only as an aggregate figure in third-party profiles.

why_it_matters: Buyer-side mapping from employer bodies will require event attendee lists, board rosters and press rather than a directory scrape.

description: No full German AHK (Delegacija njemačke privrede) chamber exists for Montenegro; searching in sr and de-adjacent terms only returned AHK Croatia/Bosnia.

result.result_summary: The German business presence is the German-Montenegrin Business Club (njemackiposlovniklub.me) plus the German embassy's economic pages.

why_it_matters: Expectations of an AHK-grade member directory and market reports for ME should be reset; the club is smaller and less document-productive.

description: No publicly posted committee/board minutes (zapisnici sa sjednica odbora) were located for either the PKCG banking board or the PKCG ICT board.

result.result_summary: Only board composition, secretary contacts and news write-ups of sessions are public; minutes appear to be internal.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed minutes would surface vendor presentations; in ME that intelligence must instead be recovered from Glasnik write-ups and news items, or requested from board secretaries.
